title: Best Payroll Software for Small Business in 2026
summary: Compare the 7 best payroll software options for small business, and which platform fits single-location, multi-state, and benefits-focused teams.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** For most small businesses that don’t plan to grow past a handful of employees and run payroll in more than one state, Gusto and QuickBooks Payroll are easy entry points. But if you have employees in more than one state, hourly and tipped staff, or you’re growing fast enough that compliance mistakes could actually hurt you, Warp, Patriot Software, and Justworks each solve a different version of that problem. If you also need core HR features (onboarding, org chart, benefits) without buying a separate HR system, Warp and Paychex bundle that in.


## What Small Businesses Actually Need From Payroll Software


A 12-person marketing agency, a 3-location coffee shop chain, and a dental practice with hourly hygienists all search on Google for the same thing, but they need different things from payroll software. Here’s what separates a good fit from a bad one.


**Most small businesses pay people in different ways** . You might have salaried managers, hourly workers, tipped employees, and a few 1099 contractors on the same payroll. Overtime, tip credits, and minimum wage rules change by state and city, and mistakes can lead to Department of Labor complaints, not just unhappy employees.


**You don’t have a dedicated payroll administrator.** At a company this size, payroll is usually one more thing the owner or office manager does on top of everything else. The software needs to work without someone first needing to read[IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p15.pdf) .


**When you open a second location or hire someone in a new city or state, you often need to register for new state tax accounts. This can include state unemployment, withholding** , and sometimes local taxes. Many small business owners get stuck here, not because payroll is complicated, but because government websites are often confusing and slow.


**Missing a filing can be expensive.** Late deposits or missed quarterly filings lead to penalties from the IRS and state agencies. If your payroll software doesn’t handle this for you, you’re responsible for catching these issues.


## The 7 Best Payroll Software Options for Small Business in 2026


We evaluated pricing, tax filing accuracy, multi-state support, and support quality across the platforms small business owners usually compare.


### 1. Warp: Best for Multi-State, Compliance-Heavy Small Businesses (and Teams That Want HR Built In)


Warp is an AI-native payroll and HR platform built for companies that can’t afford to get tax registration wrong. Instead of routing you to a state’s .gov website when you hire someone new, Warp’s AI agents open the required state tax accounts automatically and file the ongoing returns. When a tax notice arrives, Warp’s agents resolve the majority of them directly with the agency instead of forwarding the letter to you so that you are stuck handling it.​


Warp also handles employee onboarding, org charts, and[benefits](https://www.warp.co/benefits) , so small businesses don’t need a separate HR tool to manage new hires, offer letters, and benefits.


**Pricing:** Starts at $35 per employee per month, with no separate per-state filing fees.


**Best for:** Small businesses with employees in more than one state, businesses that have been burned by a tax notice before, teams that want payroll and basic HR in one place, or owners who want a real person to talk to instead of a support ticket queue.


### 2. Gusto: Best for Simple, Single-State Payroll (and Teams That Plan to Stay Small)


Gusto is still the go-to choice for small businesses with employees in one state and simple needs. Its interface is easy to use, and the Simple plan covers the basics at a good price.


**Pricing:** Starts around $40 per month plus roughly $6 per employee for the base plan; multi-state support requires an upgrade to a higher tier.


**Best for:** A single-location small business with all employees working in one state.


For a deeper comparison, see our full[Gusto alternatives breakdown](https://www.warp.co/blog/top-3-gusto-alternatives-for-scaling-startups) .


### 3. QuickBooks Payroll: Best If You’re Already on QuickBooks


If your business already uses QuickBooks Online for accounting, QuickBooks Payroll (now called QuickBooks Workforce) is a good choice. Payroll data goes straight into your accounting, so you don’t need a separate integration step.


**Pricing:** Plans generally start in the $45 to $50 per month range plus roughly $6 to $8 per employee, with higher tiers adding same-day deposit and workers’ comp administration. QuickBooks has adjusted pricing more than once in 2026, so confirm current rates before you commit.​


**Best for:** Small businesses that already use QuickBooks Online for accounting and want payroll in the same system.​


### 4. Patriot Software: Best Budget Option for Single-State Teams


Patriot is the most affordable full-service payroll option that includes tax filing, and it usually costs about half as much as Gusto for a small team.


**Pricing:** Basic Payroll (you file your own taxes) starts at $17 per month plus $4 per employee. Full Service Payroll (Patriot files for you) starts at $37 per month plus $5 per employee, with an additional $12 per month for each extra state.


**Best for:** A very small, single-state team on a tight budget that doesn’t need benefits administration or HR tools bundled in.


### 5. ADP RUN: Best for Businesses That Want an Established Name


ADP is a well-known name among small business owners, and RUN is its product for small businesses. It manages state unemployment insurance well and connects with ADP’s larger HR tools if your business grows.


**Pricing:** Not published. You’ll need a sales call for a quote, and pricing typically scales with add-ons.


**Best for:** Owners who want an established, well-known provider and don’t mind a sales conversation to get pricing.


### 6. Paychex Flex: Best for Businesses That Want Bundled HR Services


Paychex Flex combines payroll with a wide range of HR add-ons, like recruiting tools and employee handbooks. This is helpful for small businesses that want one provider for all HR needs.


**Pricing:** Quote-based; total cost depends heavily on which add-ons you select.


**Best for:** Small businesses that want a single vendor to cover payroll plus a wide range of HR services, and are comfortable negotiating pricing.


### 7. Justworks: Best for Access to Big-Company Benefits


Justworks is a[Professional Employer Organization (PEO)](https://www.warp.co/blog/do-startups-really-need-a-peo-or-eor-for-payroll) , which means it co-employs your workers so you can access large-group insurance rates that aren’t available to small businesses on their own.


**Pricing:** Typically $59 to $109 per employee per month, depending on the plan.


**Best for:** A small business competing for talent that needs enterprise-grade health insurance and 401(k) options to attract candidates.​

## How to Choose


**You’re a single-location business with everyone in one state.** Gusto or Patriot Software are the easiest, most affordable starting points. Choose Patriot if budget is the deciding factor; choose Gusto if you want the more polished interface.​


**You have employees in more than one state, or you’re growing fast.** Warp is built specifically for this. Automatic state tax registration and AI-driven notice resolution remove the two biggest sources of small business payroll headaches.


**You want payroll and HR in one system without buying two tools.** Warp and Paychex both bundle HR features; Warp includes them by default, while Paychex adds them as paid add-ons.


**You need to compete on benefits.** Justworks’ PEO model gives you access to large-group insurance rates you couldn’t get on your own, at a higher per-employee cost.


## So, which payroll software is best?


There’s no single “best” payroll software for every small business; the right choice depends on how many states you operate in, whether you need HR features alongside payroll, and whether you can afford to spend an hour on hold with a state tax agency if something goes wrong.
